# Brain Memory

> A hierarchical, file-system-based memory system for AI coding agents, inspired by human neuroscience — memories decay on an Ebbinghaus curve, strengthen through recall, connect via associative networks, and consolidate during a sleep cycle. A deterministic recall engine gives identical scoring across Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenAI Codex CLI, and OpenCode: one brain, any model, every agent.

Brain Memory stores every memory as a human-readable Markdown file with YAML frontmatter in a single global `~/.brain/` directory — no database, no server. It is free and open source (npm package: `brain-memory`).

## Getting Started

- [Overview](https://brainmemory.ai/docs): Introduction to Brain Memory — a neuroscience-inspired memory system for AI coding agents.
- [Installation](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/getting-started/installation): Install the Brain Memory plugin for Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, OpenCode, and Antigravity — or add the hosted MCP connector.
- [Quick Start](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/getting-started/quick-start): Get up and running with Brain Memory in under 5 minutes.
- [Use Brain in Claude apps](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/getting-started/claude-apps): Recall your brain from Claude on the web, desktop, and your phone via the Brain connector (remote MCP).

## Concepts

- [Memory Types](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/concepts/memory-types): Learn about the 8 memory types: decision, insight, goal, experience, learning, relationship, preference, and observation.
- [Cognitive Types](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/concepts/cognitive-types): Understand episodic, semantic, and procedural memory — modeled after human cognition.
- [Strength & Decay](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/concepts/strength-decay): How memories strengthen through recall and weaken over time via exponential decay.
- [Associative Network](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/concepts/associative-network): Memories connect via weighted edges with spreading activation and Hebbian learning.
- [Context-Dependent Recall](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/concepts/context-recall): Memories encoded in a similar context to the current session are scored higher during recall.
- [Salience & Confidence](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/concepts/salience-confidence): Emotional significance and epistemic certainty scores that influence memory behavior.
- [Provenance & Trust](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/concepts/provenance-trust): Every memory is labelled by origin, and origin bounds what it may claim — at write time and at recall.
- [Pinned Memory](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/concepts/pinned-memory): Pin critical conventions and preferences to the always-present tier — loaded every session, never decaying.
- [Procedural Skills](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/concepts/procedural-skills): Reusable how-to workflows served via progressive disclosure and learned from repeated experience.

## Commands

- [remember](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/commands/remember): Recall relevant memories using spreading activation and context-dependent scoring.
- [memorize](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/commands/memorize): Store new memories from the current session context with automatic categorization.
- [status](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/commands/status): Dashboard with brain health overview, memory counts, and strength distribution.
- [pin](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/commands/pin): Pin a memory to the always-present tier — loaded every session, never decaying. Toggles: also unpins.
- [forget](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/commands/forget): Decay or archive memories. With --deep, performs forensic erasure — traces and removes every reference.
- [import](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/commands/import): Cold-start a brain from transcripts your agents already wrote. Incremental — safe to re-run.
- [sync](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/commands/sync): Sync via Brain Cloud, Git remote, or export/import (auto-initializes the brain on first run).
- [skill](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/commands/skill): Manage procedural skills — reusable how-to workflows with progressive disclosure.
- [verify](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/commands/verify): Review and resolve memories pending verification — writes from untrusted sources held in quarantine.
- [sleep](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/commands/sleep): Full maintenance cycle: replay, homeostasis, consolidation, review reinforcement, pruning, and REM dreaming. Usually runs in the background.

## Advanced

- [Scoring Formula](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/advanced/scoring-formula): The v4 recall scoring formula: relevance, decayed strength, recency, spreading bonus, context match, and salience.
- [Spaced Reinforcement](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/advanced/spaced-reinforcement): How recall spacing affects strength boosts and decay rate improvements.
- [Sleep Cycle](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/advanced/sleep-cycle): Deep dive into the sleep maintenance cycle: replay, homeostasis, crystallization, and dreaming.
- [Cross-Agent Sharing](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/advanced/cross-agent): Share memories across Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, OpenCode, and Antigravity agents.
- [Portable Sync](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/advanced/portable-sync): Git-based sync and encrypted export/import for cross-device memory portability.
- [Working Memory & Session Start](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/advanced/working-memory): How Brain feeds the context window at session start through a single budget-bounded aggregator that never overflows working memory.
- [Portable Skill Distribution](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/advanced/skill-distribution): Ship Brain as a portable agentskills.io SKILL.md folder that runs unmodified across Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, and more.

## Reference

- [File Structure](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/reference/file-structure): Complete reference for the ~/.brain/ directory layout and file organization.
- [Memory File Format](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/reference/memory-format): YAML frontmatter schema and Markdown body format for memory files.
- [Configuration](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/reference/configuration): Configuration options for decay rates, scoring weights, and sync settings.
- [Changelog](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/reference/changelog): Release history and version notes for the Brain Memory plugin.

## Benchmarks

- [Overview](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/benchmarks): Controlled benchmark suite proving Brain Memory improves retrieval, contradiction handling, and token efficiency for AI coding agents.
- [Methodology](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/benchmarks/methodology): How retrieval is scored, why the judge is cross-family, distractor haystacks, and references to the 2025-2026 SOTA the design follows.
- [Scenarios](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/benchmarks/scenarios): The six benchmark scenarios — each describable in one sentence — with project fixtures, rubrics, and arm matrices.
- [Results](https://brainmemory.ai/docs/benchmarks/results): Current measurements from the benchmark suite, with raw JSON downloads.

## Blog

- [We tried to add embeddings. Our own benchmark said no.](https://brainmemory.ai/blog/we-tried-embeddings) (2026-09-07): A real embedding model, given every advantage, failed to beat BM25 on a 1,021-memory corpus with 1,000 distractors. Here is the experiment, the numbers, and what would change our mind.
- [When a memory stops being true](https://brainmemory.ai/blog/when-a-memory-stops-being-true) (2026-08-08): Decay handles memories that fade. It doesn't handle memories that were true and then, on a specific day, weren't. Brain now models truth-based invalidation: supersede the old fact, keep it answerable, let the new one win.
- [One skill, every agent: Brain as a portable SKILL.md](https://brainmemory.ai/blog/one-skill-every-agent) (2026-08-08): Brain already installed natively into a handful of coding agents. Now it ships as a single portable Agent Skill folder that runs unmodified across ~40 clients — the ones we support, and the ones we've never heard of.
- [Closing the loop on memory poisoning: quarantine, audit, and rollback](https://brainmemory.ai/blog/quarantine-and-audit) (2026-08-07): The write-path gate stopped planted memories from entrenching. Now brain flags untrusted writes for review, detects the patterns an attack leaves behind, and can roll the whole brain back — all five OWASP ASI06 layers, shipped.
- [Introducing Brain Memory: a memory system that forgets on purpose](https://brainmemory.ai/blog/introducing-brain-memory) (2026-07-26): AI agents start every session at zero. The usual fixes treat memory as storage plus search. Brain models it the way remembering actually works — decay, reinforcement, association — in plain files you can read.
- [Provenance, not filtering: hardening brain against memory poisoning](https://brainmemory.ai/blog/provenance-memory-poisoning) (2026-07-26): A single email can plant a false memory in an AI agent and keep it there. Here is the attack, where brain was exposed, and the write-path gate we shipped in response.
